Géniale la vidéo, First, you undermine your arguments about numbers when you talk about billions of robots then cite Amazon's sub-1 million worker count. Robots move slowly (right now), but they don't stop (take breaks/ screw around), so equivalent to 8 shift per day? More? Less? To go beyond the warehouse, with its well-defined command hierarchy, a LOT of thorny problems need to be addressed. Even Asimov's robot novels never addressed most of them. The obvious one is, who does a robot obey? Can the kids on the street order the robot working in my yard to run into traffic or go to the store for blinker fluid? AI safety efforts seem focused on preventing crimes-no-matter-who-orders-it, but what if I tell a robot to fetch me the painting in your living room. Does it obey any human? Does it obey a robot? Does it obey a playback of a recording? Does it understand who owns what, and who should be given possession? This isn't binary: I may let my toddler son order breakfast for the robot, but I don't want the robot giving that son knives... or Tide Pods for snack time either, for that matter. So, I personally think we are decades away from the general-purpose house slave... which, be honest, is what this is a about. Forget Elon's 20k bot from the individual. He might build them, but they'll be so limited that only fans will get one. For the foreseeable future, humanoid robots will be limited to very repetitive tasks in very controlled settings, and I can see a few million of those being produced. As for the rest: smarts alone won't cut it. To deploy everywhere, someone will first have to discover a Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil that a robot can ingest. Hopefully they can find the one humans can consume as well; the species seems to need booster dose., Our Robot Overlords! 😂]
